prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1180; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a low-speed collision in a retail parking lot. Insured vehicle reported as struck while reversing. Claimant vehicle is a sedan with rear bumper damage. Police report not filed; both parties exchanged information at scene. Initial photos requested from insured and claimant.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. Attorney letter received requesting that all further contact be routed through their office. Claimant reports neck and back strain following the impact and has been seen at an urgent care facility. Medical records requested through counsel. Liability appears disputed on the question of which vehicle was backing up.

Entry 3: Spoke with defense side of the file regarding the recorded statement from the insured. Insured states the claimant vehicle was moving slowly through the lane and made contact with the rear quarter panel. Parking lot security camera footage was requested from the property owner. Footage retention window noted as limited, so follow-up scheduled promptly.

Entry 4: Received preliminary records from the urgent care visit documenting cervical and lumbar strain, muscle spasm, and a prescription for anti-inflammatories and physical therapy referral. Claimant's counsel indicated a demand package is being prepared. Reserve reviewed in light of the injury documentation and the open liability question. Independent appraisal of the claimant vehicle assigned.

Entry 5: Parking lot footage obtained from property management and reviewed. Footage shows partial view of both vehicles but does not clearly capture the moment of contact. Counsel notified that the footage has been secured. Physical therapy progress reports requested from the claimant's provider through counsel. Claim remains open pending liability determination and medical review.
